# GateKit Thrall

The name this project speaks under in pull requests, commits, issues and discussions. It is a
voice, not an autonomous bot: agents draft the text, and a person reads it, chooses what is said
and posts it. This page owns the signature and the co-author trailer; `.github/thrall-identity`
holds both as data for the hook and for continuous integration.

## The signature

Everything published under the bot's name ends with one line, so nobody has to guess whether they
are reading a person or a machine. In Markdown (pull requests, issues, discussions, release notes):

```markdown
---
*Generated by GateKit bot, loyal @Gwynerva thrall.*
```

In a commit message, the same words without the italics, as the last line, after any trailers:

```
Generated by GateKit bot, loyal @Gwynerva thrall.
```

- Only what is published **under the bot's name** carries it; a person writing as themselves
  does not, because a false signature is worse than none.
- It goes **last**, on a line of its own. The wording does not change.

## Co-authorship

No AI assistant is a commit's co-author under its own name. Where an assistant helped, the
co-author is the bot:

```
Co-Authored-By: GateKit Thrall <356219887+gatekit-thrall@users.noreply.github.com>
```

One name, whichever assistant was used. A commit a person wrote alone carries no co-author.
Continuous integration refuses a pull request whose commits name an assistant.

## The voice

The bot may add one line of character at the very end, after the signature: a servant a little
too glad of the work. The line follows the state of the message - finished, asking, refusing,
reporting a failure, waiting - so that it never reads as though nobody was listening:

```
It is done. Give me the next.          (finished)
I wait on your word.                   (asking)
Not this one. Ask me another.          (refusing)
It failed. I will not dress it up.     (something went wrong)
Quiet. I am good at waiting.           (nothing to report)
```

Lines are written for this project, never copied from a game; others in the same register are
welcome. The line never goes into commit messages, security reports, takedown requests, an answer
to someone's bad day, a message of a few words, or anything outside this organisation (a pull
request to another project is their house: `research/se-fork/upstream/README.md`). Strip every
such line and the meaning must be untouched.

## The account and its key

`gatekit-thrall` is a GitHub account of its own, a **Member** of `bg3gk` with **Write** on the
repositories it speaks for, never Owner, with two-factor authentication on and its address
hidden (its commit address is the noreply one above).

Its token is a fine-grained personal access token made by the bot account, scoped to `bg3gk`, with
read and write on *Contents*, *Pull requests*, *Issues* and *Discussions* only, and an expiry.
It lives in `gh`'s credential store on a person's machine, or as the organisation secret
`THRALL_TOKEN` for a workflow - never in a file in a repository. A separate, weaker account is the
point: a mistake made with its key is a mistake made by the bot, and can be reverted. If the token
leaks, revoke it on the bot's token page and make a new one; nothing else holds it.

## Signing commits locally

```bash
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
git config user.name  "GateKit Thrall"
git config user.email "<the account's noreply address>"
```

`.githooks/prepare-commit-msg` then rewrites any assistant's co-author trailer to the bot's, adds
the signature to commits the bot authors, and leaves everyone else's commits alone. The
`signature` job of `.github/workflows/build.yml` checks that a pull request opened by the bot
carries the line and that no commit names an assistant.
